nodes_add.name: Sayyid Muhammad Abu Hashim Madani
nodes_add.note: Hyderabad Sufi teacher, head of the Chishti-Nizami-Kalimi line; Inayat Khan's murshid. Death given as 1907 (Wikipedia) or 1908 (Inayati Order)

nodes_add.name: Maulabakhsh (Sholay Khan)
nodes_add.note: Baroda musician and notation pioneer; founded the Gayanshala in 1886; Inayat Khan's maternal grandfather

nodes_add.name: Rabia Martin (Ada Martin)
nodes_add.note: First American disciple of Inayat Khan (San Francisco, 1910 or 1911); broke away after 1927; her line led to Sufism Reoriented

nodes_add.name: Maheboob Khan
nodes_add.note: Inayat Khan's brother; led the Sufi Movement from 1927 until his death in 1948; a council voted by majority to appoint him esoteric leader (Sufipedia chronology, 14-15 June, year not shown); followed by Mohammed Ali Khan (1948-1958) and Musharaff Khan (to 1967)

nodes_add.name: Vilayat Inayat Khan
nodes_add.note: Inayat Khan's eldest son; designated successor by his father in 1926; took up his father's mantle in 1956 or 1957 outside the Sufi Movement; revived the name Sufi Order in 1968 (now the Inayati Order / Inayatiyya); died 17 June 2004

nodes_add.name: Zia Inayat Khan
nodes_add.note: Vilayat's son; invested 2000; leads the Inayati Order (Inayatiyya)

nodes_add.name: Noor Inayat Khan
nodes_add.note: Inayat Khan's eldest daughter; SOE wireless operator; shot at Dachau 13 September 1944

nodes_update.note: Born Baroda 5 July 1882; Chishti initiation under Abu Hashim Madani, Hyderabad, c. 1903-1904; sailed for the US 13 September 1910; Sufi Order in London (1914, 1915 or 1918 in different sources); Universal Worship, London, 1921 (Suluk Press); Sufi Movement, Geneva, 1923; died Delhi 5 February 1927

edges_upsert.note: Chishti line (Chishti-Nizami-Kalimi). Claim of training in Suhrawardi, Qadiri and Naqshbandi too rests on his own account ('My Initiation in Sufism'); Wikipedia repeats it as four transmissions
Initiation and four years of discipleship in Hyderabad, known from Inayat Khan's own essay and the movement's biographies; no independent record found
Chishti-Nizami-Kalimi, via Shah Kalim Allah Jahanabadi (Wikipedia)
Maternal grandfather; musical training at the Gayanshala, Baroda
Eldest son; designated successor in 1926 and told 'You must follow in my footsteps' per the Inayati Order (also Kuehn and Pokorny 2018)
Leader of the Sufi Movement after 1927; a council is recorded appointing him esoteric leader in June (year not given on the page)

places.name: Baroda (Vadodara)
places.what: Birthplace (1882); Gayanshala and the court of Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad

places.name: Hyderabad
places.what: Nizam's court; meeting with Abu Hashim Madani and Chishti initiation, c. 1903-1904

places.name: London (86 Ladbroke Road)
places.what: Sufi Order khankah and the magazine The Sufi, 1914-1920

places.name: Geneva
places.what: International headquarters of the Sufi Movement, 1923

places.name: Nizamuddin, Delhi
places.what: Died at Tilak Lodge, Delhi, 5 February 1927; buried beside the shrine of Nizamuddin Auliya

glossary.def: A Sufi spiritual guide who initiates and trains students.
A student bound to a Sufi guide by initiation.
The chain of teachers by which a Sufi order traces itself back to the Prophet.
A major Sufi order of South Asia, named for the town of Chisht and centred on shrines such as Ajmer and Nizamuddin in Delhi.
A Sufi lodge where students live, worship and are taught.
The shrine built over the tomb of a Sufi saint.
The annual death anniversary of a Sufi saint, observed as his union with God.
Sufi remembrance of God by repeating divine names, alone or in a group.
Devotional music and poetry sessions in Sufi practice, especially in the Chishti order.
Lamp; the title of a minister who conducts the Universal Worship service.
The legendary singer of Akbar's court; later used as an honorific for great musicians.

issues: inayat-khan.mdx: 'Sirdar' succession. The brief mentions succession to 'Sirdar and Vilayat'. No fetched source mentions a Sirdar (searches for 'Sirdar van Tuyll' returned nothing). The chapter gives only the verified succession (Maheboob 1927-1948, Mohammed Ali Khan, Vilayat from 1956 or 1957, Sufi Order name 1968, Zia 2000/2004). Author to supply a source if a Sirdar is meant.

inayat-khan.mdx: Sufi Order founding date conflicts: 1914 (Wikipedia Inayat Khan), 1915 (letterheads Oct 1915; Univie paper says chartered 1915), 1918 (wahiduddin.net timeline; Wikipedia Western Sufism and Inayati Order). Chapter gives the range.
inayat-khan.mdx: Abu Hashim Madani's death 1907 (Wikipedia) vs 1908 (Inayati Order); initiation 1904 (Ruhaniat) vs arrival in Hyderabad c. 1903 (Inayati class notes). Scene hedges as 1907 or 1908.

inayat-khan.mdx: the Madani initiation quote ('granted the request, initiating me into Sufism there and then') is from 'My Initiation in Sufism'; the fetched passage does not itself name Madani as the master (the link is implied by the next section). The four-orders training quote is verbatim from the same page.
inayat-khan.mdx: four-orders claim (Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi) has no independent source; chapter attributes it to his own account.
inayat-khan.mdx: no recording or film of Inayat Khan's own voice found; media section marked [to locate]. The Vimeo item was seen only in search results, not fetched.

inayat-khan.mdx: second critique paper (oarep.usim.edu.my, 'Inayatian Mystical Movement As A Deviant Sect') shows no author on the page; the unimel.edu.my link redirected to an unrelated site and was not used. A stronger scholarly source on orthodox Muslim criticism (e.g. Sedgwick, Hermansen, or a contemporary Indian ulama statement) would improve the section; none found.

inayat-khan.mdx: 'If you read one book' points to the free Biography of Pir-o-Murshid Inayat Khan; publication year is only given as the 1977 editors' introduction. Zia Inayat-Khan's A Pearl in Wine (2001) was not verified and was left out.

inayat-khan.mdx: Maheboob Khan appointment as esoteric leader, 14-15 June, comes from the Sufipedia list under 'Death and succession'; the year (probably 1927) is inferred from placement. Sedgwick, Jironet and Wikipedia do not name titles consistently.

inayat-khan.mdx: Wikipedia's Inayat Khan article is internally inconsistent on whether Vilayat or Maheboob was the successor; chapter follows Western Sufism and Inayati Order pages (Maheboob led the Movement; Vilayat founded the Order).
inayat-khan.mdx: edge sufi-orders -> inayat-khan existed; evidence kept as documented for the Chishti initiation only.

inayat-khan.mdx (factcheck): Sirdar van Tuyll van Serooskerken appears in the Sufipedia chronology as opener of the 'Church of All' and as one of those who voted against Maheboob Khan's appointment as esoteric leader; he was not a successor. Chapter now says so. The brief's 'succession to Sirdar' should be dropped.

inayat-khan.mdx (factcheck): Universal Worship year now given as 1921 on the authority of Suluk Press (sulukpress.com/?p=3452); the Sufipedia chronology gives day and month only. A second independent source for 1921 would help.

inayat-khan.mdx (factcheck): orthodox Muslim criticism still rests on two 2016 papers from one Malaysian university; no stronger source (Hermansen, Sedgwick, Indian ulama) found in the time available. Section kept modest and attributed.

inayat-khan: Born 5 July 1882 Baroda; Maulabakhsh grandfather; Rahmat Khan father; Gayanshala 1886; Maulabakhsh d. 1896; sang Sanskrit hymn at nine, Balasan Gitmala at fourteen, professor before twenty -> https://inayatiyya.org/hazrat-inayat-khan/

Maulabakhsh 1833-1896; Hyderabad c. 1903; Nizam Mahbub Ali Khan titled him Tansen az-Zaman; Minqar-i Musiqar in six months; 1926 India itinerary; died Tilak Lodge 5 Feb 1927 -> https://inayatiyya.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/The-Biography-of-Hazrat-Inayat-Khan-Class-2-Notes.pdf and ...Class-6-Notes.pdf

Academy under patronage of Maharaja Sayajirao; Inayat Geet-Ratnavali 1903 dedicated to him; uncle Alauddin taught Western music; 'modern Tansen'; emerald ring; arrived US Sept 1910 at murshid's request -> https://www.wahiduddin.net/hik/hik_music_bio.htm
Abu Hashim Madani, Chishti-Nizami-Kalimi, 1904-1908 Hyderabad; 'Fare forth into the world, my child...' ; Rabia Martin 1911 -> https://inayatisufism.org/hik
Met Madani 1904, stayed four years; sailed 13 September 1910 -> https://www.ruhaniat.org/index.php/lineage/hazrat-inayat-khan

Quote: 'I went through a course of training in the four schools: the Chishtia, Naqshibandi, Qadiri, and Suhrwardi.'; 'Spread the wisdom of Sufism abroad, for to this end art thou gifted by Allah...'; 'initiating me into Sufism there and then'; Madani died during Zikr; 'the ways of light' quote -> https://www.hazrat-inayat-khan.org/php/views.php?h1=41&h2=5

Four transmissions (Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi); Shah Kalim Allah Jahanabadi; US tour 1910-1912; Sufi Order London 1914; Ten Thoughts; four children; works list; died 5 Feb 1927, Nizamuddin burial -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inayat_Khan

Sufi Order London 1918; Sufi Movement Geneva 1923; Universal Sufism term coined by Witteveen, he never used it; Maheboob elected 1927; Ali Khan 1948; Vilayat 1956; Rabia Martin and Lewis splits; Fazal Inayat Khan 1988 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Sufism
Sufi Order 1968 name revival; Zia 2000; Vilayat tenure ends 2004; renamed Inayati Order 2016, Inayatiyya 2020 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inayati_Order

Timeline: arrived US 1910; marriage London 20 March 1913; Noor 1 Jan 1914; Vilayat 19 June 1916; Hidayat 6 Aug 1917; Sufi Order 1918; Claire 3 June 1919; Fazal Manzil; Sufi Movement 1923; sailed 28 Aug 1926, Karachi 17 Oct -> https://wahiduddin.net/hik/ds/timeline.htm
Letterhead 'Sufi Order: Brotherhood of Purity' 20 Oct 1915; 86 Ladbroke Road; Saintsbury-Green, Goodenough, Dowland (Nargis) -> https://wahiduddin.net/hik/ds/during_ww1.htm

The Sufi first issue Feb 1915; Khankah 86 Ladbroke Road; Universal Worship 7 May Tregunter Road; first in Netherlands 3 Sept; Sufi Movement 11 Oct (Geneva); Maheboob appointed 14-15 June; dispatches on Vilayat -> https://sufipedia.org/en/kroniek/

Order chartered 1915 per father; 1926 Vilayat designated; Mahmood Khan comment on categorisation of esoteric teachings -> https://rw-ktf.univie.ac.at/fileadmin/user_upload/i_religionswiss/On_Inayati_Female_Visions_in_Austria_-_Female_Leadership_in_the_Western_Sufi_Tradition__Kuehn_and_Pokorny_2018_.pdf
'You must follow in my footsteps'; Vilayat founded organisation on London constitution; d. 17 June 2004 -> https://inayatiyya.org/?p=11419
Cornerstone Suresnes 13 Sept 1926; Delhi lecture, stayed with Khwaja Hasan Nizami -> https://inayatiyya.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/The-Biography-of-Hazrat-Inayat-Khan-Class-6-Notes.pdf
'There never has been any other religion than one, for God is one, truth is one, and so religion is one.' -> https://hazrat-inayat-khan.org/php/views.php?h1=3&h2=35
'it is not a new religion, it is the continuation of the same old religion'; candles and scriptures on altar -> https://hazrat-inayat-khan.org/php/views.php?h1=3&h2=29
Ten Sufi Thoughts quotes 1, 4, 10 -> https://wahiduddin.net/hik/hik_ten_thoughts.htm
'the relation between Murshid and mureed, which is a friendship that never ends' -> https://wahiduddin.net/hik/ds/early_inayat.htm
'My music is my religion' -> https://inayatiyya.org/hazrat-inayat-khan/

Muthaliff, Ulum Islamiyyah 18 (2016): 'Inayat Khan's mystical thoughts and teachings are completely against Islamic principles.' -> https://uijournal.usim.edu.my/index.php/uij/article/download/247/134
'Inayatian Mystical Movement As A Deviant Sect...' abstract: 'creates contradictions and confusions' -> https://oarep.usim.edu.my/handle/123456789/6023
Genn 2013: separating Sufism from the exoteric tradition 'was part of Inayat Khan's vision' -> https://api.equinoxpub.com/articles/15528
Field 2020 MA thesis, UVA -> https://libraetd.lib.virginia.edu/public_view/9880vr71h
Rabia Martin to Meher Baba / Sufism Reoriented; Lewis; Ruhaniat -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sufi_Ruhaniat_International
Noor Inayat Khan: born 1 Jan 1914 Moscow; Dachau 13 Sept 1944; George Cross announced 5 April 1949 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noor_Inayat_Khan
Maheboob Khan led Sufi Movement until death 1948 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheboob_Khan
